gate_notes: The model does not significantly outperform the following baseline(s) at p<0.05: ['predict_zero', 'global_median', 'trailing_12', 'sector_mean']. For a pre-apply, no-demand forecast this humble result is EXPECTED (D5-01) — a low R² is a feature, not a bug. The model card states this plainly; no features/folds/tests were tuned to cross the gate.

anchor_audit.source_field: pre-open anchor allocation book size (₹ crore)

limitations.title: A humble R² is the honest result
limitations.body: This is a pre-apply, no-demand forecast made at issue open (T0). It cannot see book-build demand, so a low out-of-sample R² is EXPECTED — a feature, not a bug (D5-01). A high R² (> 0.5) would instead flag a T0-violating feature leaking the future, so it is wired as a release-gate alarm.

limitations.title: Coverage is measured, not assumed
limitations.body: The 80% interval coverage is the REAL held-out number over IPOs the model never trained on. It can land below or above 0.80 — the card shows the measured value, never a rounded-to-0.80 fiction (P17).

limitations.title: The PIT curve is grid-derived
limitations.body: The reliability/PIT diagnostic fits a fine 0.05..0.95 quantile grid PURELY for the plot; the production interval stays the 0.1 / 0.5 / 0.9 band. The PIT is labelled grid-derived wherever it is shown (A8).

limitations.title: The Diebold–Mariano test is cross-sectional
limitations.body: The four baselines are compared under the identical as-of-T0 protocol, but the loss differential is cross-sectional across IPOs rather than a single time series — read the DM p-values with that caveat (A7). A paired Wilcoxon signed-rank p is reported alongside as a distribution-free cross-check.

limitations.title: Seed provenance — regenerates at the live build
limitations.body: These numbers are assembled from the current seed/fixture artifacts so the card and its plots render offline today. They regenerate from the live walk-forward over the real survivorship panel at the 05-11 checkpoint.
